spotlights.label: No signal when hints are ignored
spotlights.why: send_early_hints returns None whether it sent a hint or skipped it. Hypercorn advertises the extension only on HTTP/2 and HTTP/3, and TestClient never advertises it, so a TestClient test always takes the silent path.

spotlights.label: Link values are sent unvalidated
spotlights.why: Each value is only encoded as latin-1: a non-latin-1 URL raises UnicodeEncodeError, and CR/LF or a malformed Link value is passed to the server unchecked. Header validation is left to the ASGI server.

spotlights.label: HTTPEndpoint push promises now send
spotlights.why: Before, the Request in HTTPEndpoint and in a BaseHTTPMiddleware dispatch had no send channel, so send_push_promise raised "Send channel has not been made available". Now it sends, or no-ops. Code that relied on that error behaves differently.

spotlights.label: A hint after response start crashes the middleware
spotlights.why: Nothing checks that http.response.start has not gone out yet. Behind BaseHTTPMiddleware, a hint sent from a streaming body lands in body_stream and fails its "Unexpected message" assertion. Hypercorn sends a 103 only before the response starts.

steps.title: Add Request.send_early_hints
steps.why: A new method on Request takes one required Link value plus any more, positional-only. If the scope advertises http.response.early_hint, it encodes them as latin-1 and sends one http.response.early_hint event through the Request's send channel; otherwise it does nothing.
steps.consequence: Plain function routes can send a 103 right away, since request_response already builds Request with send. HTTPEndpoint and BaseHTTPMiddleware can't yet.

notes: async def send_early_hints(self, link: str, /, *additional_links: str)
Only encoding: no Link syntax check

steps.title: Give HTTPEndpoint and middleware requests a send channel
steps.why: HTTPEndpoint.dispatch now builds its Request with send=self.send. BaseHTTPMiddleware's _CachedRequest takes send as a required third argument, so the request a dispatch function sees can send too.
steps.consequence: send_early_hints (and send_push_promise) work from an HTTPEndpoint method and from a dispatch function. A hint from dispatch goes straight to the outer send.

notes: def __init__(self, scope: Scope, receive: Receive, send: Send):
Required now: private, but signature breaks
The outer send, not the stream

steps.title: Forward hints through BaseHTTPMiddleware and GZip
steps.why: call_next used to read one optional debug message and then assert http.response.start. It now loops: debug messages set info, early_hint messages are sent straight to the outer send, and the first other message ends the loop. GZipMiddleware passes early_hint through untouched, like trailers.
steps.consequence: A downstream hint reaches the client before the final response under either middleware. Before, a raw early_hint event failed the start assertion in BaseHTTPMiddleware and GZip dropped it without a word.

notes: Any number of events before start
Strict now: no info is KeyError

steps.title: Prove hints at each layer
steps.why: Unit tests cover the event shape with two links, the silent no-op without the extension, and the RuntimeError without a send channel. Integration tests check that HTTPEndpoint, BaseHTTPMiddleware (hints from dispatch and endpoint, in order) and GZipMiddleware (gzip and identity) put the hint before http.response.start.
steps.consequence: Ordering is pinned at every layer the PR touches. No test sends a hint after the response has started.
